title: Dependency risk: update, pin or replace

videos.script: linkbox depends on eight packages. It asked for two of them. {{tree}} The other six came along, and one of them reached the image without any file naming it. This lesson is about what to do with a dependency from now on. There are three moves. {{moves}} Pin it, so nothing changes unless somebody chooses. Update it, when the project is healthy and the new version is read and tested. Or replace it, when the project has said, in writing, that it will not fix what matters to you. You will compile a lock with a hash beside every file. {{lock}} You will put a date in that compile, so a release published an hour ago cannot reach it. {{date}} You will move gunicorn across four major versions, and watch a package leave the image. Then the build loses its network, and can use only what it was handed. {{offline}} Last, a package whose maintainers will not fix an advisory, and the argument for replacing it. {{replace}}
